culture.def: The shared practices, beliefs, objects and behaviors that a group of people learns and passes on to the next generation.

culture-trait.def: One single part of a culture, such as a food, a greeting, a style of house, a holiday or a way of using land.

cultural-relativism.def: Trying to understand a practice by the standards of the culture it belongs to, before judging it.

ethnocentrism.def: Judging another culture by the standards of your own culture, often seeing your own as the right or best way.

folk-culture.def: Culture kept by a small, close group, often rural, taught by family and community, and slow to change. Plain dress and barn raisings among the Amish are examples.

popular-culture.def: Culture shared by large, mixed groups of people in many places, spread by media and business, and quick to change, such as hit songs, chain restaurants and fashion.
